title.narrative: Activity under preparation Support to Strengthening Mine Action in Syria

description.narrative:
The HALO Trust¿s EU-funded project, "Support to Strengthening Mine Action in Syria", is an 18-month intervention aimed at mitigating the threat of explosive ordnance (EO), including landmines, unexploded remnants of war (ERW), and improvised explosive devices (IEDs), to enable safe returns, stabilisation, and recovery in post-conflict Syria following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024. Implementing a multi-pronged approach, the project¿led by HALO in partnership with Tech 4 Tracing (T4T) and Mines Advisory Group (MAG)¿will deploy drone-enabled surveys with AI-assisted analysis to accelerate hazard mapping, mechanical and manual clearance (including a specialised tiller/flail machine for agricultural land), explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) spot tasks, and explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) targeting 128,500 direct beneficiaries (including returnees, farmers, children, and women).

Key outputs include clearing 550,000m² of land, preparing 238,000m² via tiller, conducting 1,026 EOD callouts, and delivering EORE to 44,000 people across high-risk governorates (Idleb, Aleppo, Hama, Deir ez-Zor, and Daraa). The project integrates innovative technology (AI-driven drone imagery analysis) to enhance efficiency, while prioritising local capacity-building¿training 46 Syrian staff in drone operations, clearance, and EORE¿and aligning with emerging national structures like the National Mine Action Centre (NMAC). Sustainability is ensured through permanent hazard removal, institutional knowledge transfer, and environmental safeguards, directly supporting EU priorities on stabilisation, humanitarian disarmament (e.g., Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention), and safe, voluntary refugee returns. Coordination with UNMAS, and other mine action actors ensures complementarity and avoids duplication.
